$comment: The living record of what is tested, at which layer, and — more usefully —
what is not. A prose table in a README drifts within weeks because nothing
reads it; this file is machine-readable so `quality-matrix.test.mjs` can
check it against reality and fail when the two disagree.
Every plan that adds a feature adds or updates its row here. `covered` is
not a wish: a layer listed as covered must have a test that exists.
Layers: L1 pure logic · L2 Svelte components in jsdom · L3 backend against
temp dirs · L4 the real app driven end to end · L5 manual, on real

flows.gaps: No L3 test boots the backend against a seeded profile; the E2E journey covers the same ground end to end, which is arguably the better place for it.
No component test mounts TerminalArea. Closing a terminal from the UI is not covered — the journey asserts the panes that restore, not the ones a user closes.
Re-parenting a live xterm on a move is the risky part and has no automated coverage at all.

flows.flow: Sleep and wake a workspace, with scrollback
flows.gaps: The journey proves a sleeping workspace spawns no shells. Waking one — and whether the replayed scrollback matches what was captured — is still only checked by hand.

flows.flow: Add a project and create a worktree
flows.gaps: Clone-and-register and PR/issue adoption are covered at L1/L2; manual branch creation through the UI and WSL path routing still have no automated interaction test.
Hunk-level staging is covered in Rust but not through the UI.

The journey covers the half uxnan owns: the agent runs under a shell, the endpoint file is written, an untokened report is refused and a valid one reaches the state the sidebar reads. Whether a *particular* CLI's reporter is installed and correct is a separate question, and belongs to L5.
The engine's logic is well covered; nothing exercises it against real agent processes.

The journey opens, loads and closes a loopback page (a child webview of the main window). Switching workspace, overlays over the page and the routing preference are not covered end to end; the per-workspace store has no component test yet.
The journey boots the app over a profile shaped by an older build and asserts the projects survive. Changing a setting through the UI is not covered.

evidence.L1: src/lib/markdown.test.ts, src/lib/diffParse.test.ts (contract tests against captured real gh output in tests/fixtures/github/), scripts/github/lib.test.mjs (the sandbox allowlist + capture sanitizer), tests/github-command-inventory.test.mjs (the command inventory vs the source)
evidence.L3: src-tauri/src/github/fixture_tests.rs (production parsers against the captured real payloads), src-tauri/tests/github_cli.rs (the production runner through real child processes: merge refusals, degraded environments, .cmd resolution, env hygiene), tests/fixtures/fixtures.test.mjs (the fake gh itself, incl. scripted outcomes)

platforms.windows: read side validated on captured real data; write side offline-validated AND live-validated 2026-08-01 (supervised sandbox run, 7/7 live tests green, refusal texts re-captured)

flows.gaps: The supervised live suite ran green on 2026-08-01 (docs/github-validation.md records the run and its findings) and the opt-in E2E journey (tests/e2e/specs/github-fake.e2e.mjs, UXNAN_E2E_FAKE_GH=1) passed its first run the same day. Still open: auto-merge arm/disarm, update-branch and Actions re-run are not yet in the live suite (runbook extensions); the issue-develop dialog belongs to an on-device pass; approve/request-changes and reviewer requests need a second account (single-account limit; the refusals are covered).

evidence.L3: src-tauri/tests/automations_store.rs, src-tauri/src/automations/*.rs #[cfg(test)] (incl. the budget a run is admitted under and a cancelled step recorded as stopped)
evidence.L5: Driven by hand on macOS (2026-09-22): the headless runner executed a two-step automation with real agents — context passed between steps, output sizes and the tree's peak memory recorded, and the budget ledger empty afterwards; two runner processes with a one-agent budget took turns instead of overlapping.

platforms.macos: verified by hand (2026-09-22): headless runs, budget, capture

flows.gaps: Scheduler registration is verified manually on Windows only, and no E2E journey drives an automation through the packaged app. The budget's cross-process behavior is covered by real competing processes (tests/agent_budget.rs) but only on this platform; Windows and Linux are CI-compiled.
The overlay is a second window; multi-window E2E is unproven.
A signed-artifact round trip is L5 by nature.

flows.flow: Platform claims and the release gate

evidence.L1: tests/platform-support.test.mjs (the matrix checked against the repo + the announced-level gate), scripts/platform-support.mjs (the release-workflow gate)

flows.gaps: The L5 half is the per-platform manual checklists inside tests/platform-support.json — macOS/Linux hardware is not available, which is exactly what the matrix records.

evidence.L4: scripts/resources/run.mjs (the benchmark launches and measures the real app — 55 verified runs; it does not use WebDriver, which is why it is unaffected by the E2E attachment problem)

flows.gaps: R07/R08 need an operator; R10 (the 2 h soak) has never been run; R12 (the resource monitor's own overhead) is wired but its baseline has not been captured — the harness refuses to run beside a live uxnan instance.

evidence.L3: src-tauri/src/resources.rs #[cfg(test)] (cadence, attribution, deltas, buffer, export golden tests) plus src-tauri/tests/resources_processes.rs (real spawned process trees)

flows.gaps: No E2E journey opens the backend popover against the real binary yet (the suite cannot run beside a live uxnan instance, so it was not runnable while this feature was built); the popover lease -> sample -> park round trip is covered at L2/L3 instead. macOS/Linux metrics run the same portable sysinfo code but are unvalidated on hardware — the UI says 'best effort' there on purpose.

flows.flow: Resource mode (presets, overrides, governed consumers, auto-sleep)

evidence.L3: src-tauri/src/resources.rs #[cfg(test)] (the history budget's clamp/trim/summary), src-tauri/src/model.rs #[cfg(test)] (resource-mode settings defaults + round trip)

flows.gaps: No E2E journey switches the preset against the real binary (the same live-instance constraint as the popover journey), and the per-preset efficiency matrix (--resource-profile) is wired but unmeasured for the same reason — it must run with the app closed. Workspace auto-sleep's automatic level needs a multi-platform soak with real live processes before its feature flag can ever be retired (L5), and the maintainer's on-device review of the new Settings section is still owed.

flows.flow: Control surface (MCP tools + uxnan-cli): catalog, scope, create/converse/orchestrate, unattended launches, terminal/close, the run inbox in the console

evidence.L1: src/lib/orchestration/run.test.ts (driven runs, inbox, dispatch ids), src/lib/agentUnattended.test.ts (the per-CLI tiers, the mode detection, never a bypass flag), src-tauri/crates/control-protocol/src/catalog.rs #[cfg(test)] (every entry has a schema and an example), src-tauri/crates/control-protocol/src/private.rs #[cfg(test)] (owner-only file check), src-tauri/crates/uxnan-cli/src/main.rs #[cfg(test)] (every CLI form parses; the committed reference is current)
evidence.L2: src/lib/control/bridge.svelte.test.ts (the window bridge: create in the background, the launch budget, unattended launches, terminal/close, a coordinator's loop with questions), src/lib/components/orchestration/RunInbox.svelte.test.ts (who drives a run and what waits), src/lib/components/AgentProfileEditor.svelte.test.ts (the per-agent unattended switch)
evidence.L3: src-tauri/src/control/tests.rs (the two gates and both transports over a real socket with Tauri's mock app: catalog dispatch, scope of a launch token incl. a linked worktree outside the checkout, receipts and audit, a worktree created on a real repository, agent/wait on a real PTY, inbox wake-ups, terminal/close busy/invalid)
evidence.L5: docs/control-api.md → Verifying: driven live from inside the app on macOS — a Claude Code coordinator driving a Claude Code worker in a new worktree, an unattended Codex worker with no prompt, a worker that built the unattended-by-design branch end to end

platforms.windows: CI-compiled only (the control.json DACL and the uxnan-cli shim were written on macOS; FOR-DEV owes a run on real Windows)

flows.gaps: No E2E journey drives the packaged app through uxnan-cli (the sidecar is bundled but the wdio suite has no control-surface spec yet); the Windows ACL and the shim's uninstall are compiled by CI but unverified on a real Windows machine (FOR-DEV); Linux is untested beyond CI.

flows.flow: The global agent budget: slots across processes, the memory condition, cancellation and what a run cost

evidence.L1: src-tauri/src/budget.rs #[cfg(test)] exercised through src-tauri/tests/agent_budget.rs (the rules), src-tauri/src/automations/runner.rs #[cfg(test)] (what a mirrored budget means, clamped to the engine's bounds), src-tauri/src/model.rs #[cfg(test)] (the mirror round-trips and is optional), src/lib/state/resourceMode.svelte.test.ts (the mirror is written and reconciled), src/lib/resources/policy.test.ts (the presets)
evidence.L3: src-tauri/tests/agent_budget.rs — real competing **processes**: the cap holds between them, a killed holder's slot is reclaimed, a waiter takes the slot the moment it frees, each refusal names what was in the way. src-tauri/tests/agent_memory.rs — a real allocating process tree is measured through its children. src-tauri/src/agentrun.rs #[cfg(test)] — a real tree is killed to the grandchild, a cancelled run reports itself cancelled, and a child that outprints the capture cap still finishes.
evidence.L5: Driven by hand on macOS (2026-09-22): two headless runner processes with a one-agent budget serialized their steps (no overlap), and a step's peak tree memory landed in the run record.

platforms.windows: CI-compiled only; the ledger, the tree kill and the sampler are portable (sysinfo) but unverified there
platforms.macos: verified by hand and by test (2026-09-22)

flows.gaps: No E2E journey exercises the budget through the packaged app. The per-agent memory ceiling is advisory — measured and then stopped, never enforced by the OS; real enforcement (Job Objects, cgroups) is owed and belongs with the platform matrix. The preset memory numbers are provisional rather than measured against the low-consumption baselines.
